anchor_clauses: SOP Annex III para 3 (Suspected Money Mule Transaction)

clauses.title: Procedure and Timeline for Temporary Debit Hold, step 1
clauses.text: The bank shall place a Temporary Debit Hold on the Suspected Money Mule Transaction or, if the account is a Suspected Money Mule Account, on the entire account. Timeline: Immediately

clauses.title: Internal Policy, item (ii)
clauses.text: (ii) norms for placing temporary debit hold on amounts or account level and scenarios for its removal. The Internal Policy shall ensure that the temporary debit hold at the account level shall be applied as a last resort and only in exceptional circumstances;

clauses.title: Procedure and Timeline for Temporary Debit Hold, step 2
clauses.text: The bank shall notify the account holder of the Temporary Debit Hold, stating reasons, the process for removal, and the concerned officer's contact details, through digital mode (if mobile number / e-mail is on record) or physical mode. Timeline: On putting the temporary debit hold, the bank shall immediately notify the account holder, if communicating through digital mode, otherwise by EOD of the next day.

clauses.title: Procedure and Timeline for Removal of Temporary Debit Hold, step 3
clauses.text: The bank shall seek the explanation / justification on the genuineness of the transaction / account from the account holder. Timeline: The bank shall give 20 days’ time from the date of Temporary Debit Hold to the account holder for submission of the explanation / justification.

clauses.id: SOP Annex III para 3 (Suspected Money Mule Transaction)
clauses.title: Definition: Suspected Money Mule Transaction
clauses.text: “Suspected Money Mule Transaction” means a transaction of ₹1000 and above, flagged by the bank's transaction-monitoring systems (including AI / ML-based tools), as suspected to be proceeds of money mule activity or cyber-enabled financial fraud, based on indicators such as being unusual for or disproportionate to the account holder's declared profile; or having linkage to an account already reported as money mule or fraudulent.

clauses.title: Transactions that need close monitoring
clauses.text: 40. Without prejudice to the generality of factors that call for close monitoring, the bank shall necessarily monitor the following types of transactions: (1) Large and complex transactions including RTGS transactions, and those with unusual patterns, inconsistent with the normal and expected activity of the customer, which have no apparent economic rationale or legitimate purpose. (2) Transactions which exceed the thresholds prescribed for specific categories of accounts. (3) High account turnover inconsistent with the size of the balance maintained. (4) Deposit of third-party cheques, drafts, etc. in the existing and newly opened accounts followed by cash withdrawals for large amounts. For ongoing due diligence, the bank may consider adopting appropriate innovations including artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI and ML) technologies to support effective monitoring.

clauses.id: SOP Annex III para 3 (Money Mule Account)
clauses.title: Definition: Money Mule Account
clauses.text: “Money Mule Account” means an account used, knowingly or unknowingly, to receive, layer or transfer proceeds of cyber-enabled financial fraud on behalf of another person.

clauses.title: Operation of Bank Accounts and Money Mules
clauses.text: 68. Operation of Bank Accounts and Money Mules: The bank shall strictly adhere to the instructions on opening of accounts and monitoring of transactions, to minimise the operations of ‘Money Mules’ that are used to launder the proceeds of fraud schemes (e.g., phishing and identity theft) by criminals who gain illegal access to deposit accounts by recruiting third parties that act as ‘money mules’. The bank shall undertake diligence measures and meticulous monitoring to identify accounts which are operated as Money Mules and take appropriate action, including reporting of suspicious transactions to FIU-IND. Further, if it is established that an account opened and operated is that of a Money Mule, but STR was not filed by the concerned bank, it shall then be deemed that the bank has not complied with these directions.

## Patterns matched
- **pass_through** – Most money received is sent on.  
- **rapid_forwarding** – Money forwarded within 24 hours of arrival.  
- **linkage** – Transfers with an account already reported on NCRP.  

## Red flags and SOP basis
| Red flag | Description (from evidence) | SOP / regulatory basis |
|----------|-----------------------------|------------------------|
| Pass‑through behavior | Pass‑through ratio 0.9876 (99.76 % of inbound funds forwarded) exceeds the **pass_through_min** of 0.8 and is in the 99.7 th percentile. | The bank must place a Temporary Debit Hold on a **Suspected Money Mule Account** [**SOP Annex III para 4 step 1**]. The definition of a suspected money‑mule transaction includes “being unusual for or disproportionate to the account holder's declared profile” [**SOP Annex III para 3 (Suspected Money Mule Transaction)**]. |
| Rapid forwarding | Rapid‑forwarding metric 0.9999 (99.99 % of funds moved within 24 h) is above the 95 % top‑percentile threshold. | The hold is justified under the same provision to act on suspected money‑mule activity [**SOP Annex III para 4 step 1**] and the need to monitor large, atypical flows per the RBI monitoring guidance [**KYC-CB-2025 para 40**]. |
| Linkage to reported counter‑party | Transfer(s) involving a counter‑party already reported on the NCRP (1 reported counter‑party, 1 transfer). | Linkage to a reported account is a specific indicator for suspected money‑mule activity [**SOP Annex III para 3 (Suspected Money Mule Transaction)**]; therefore a hold is warranted. |
| Hold level justification | The typology recommends an **account‑level** hold. | Internal policy permits account‑level holds only in “exceptional circumstances” and as a “last resort” [**SOP Annex III para 6(ii)**]. The present signals satisfy that exception. |
| Notification & removal process | Upon hold, the bank must notify the holder immediately and allow 20 days for explanation. | Notification requirement [**SOP Annex III para 4 step 2**]; removal timeline [**SOP Annex III para 5 step 3**]. |
